If you have dig(1) installed (on my Arch install it's part of the bind-tools package; not sure about Mint), you could do this:

dig -t txt istheinternetonfire.com | grep --context=1 "ANSWER SECTION" | tail -1 | sed -e 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/g'

to see whether or not the internet is on fire. It reads the TXT record of the domain istheinternetonfire.org, looks for a specific part, and does a little formatting. For more fun, you could use it with cowsay(1)'s "flaming sheep" option.
